status_policy.promotion_policy: A rule is never promoted from proposal or committee review to adopted, in-force or applicable by model inference. Adoption, entry into force and application dates remain separate. A rule's jurisdiction, vessel scope, voyage scope and reporting period must be resolved for each case.
limitations: This snapshot is a research register, not legal advice or a verifier determination.
Official meeting summaries can evidence committee decisions but do not replace the adopted legal text or charted geographic boundary.
Re-fetch and review official instruments before every real reporting period; this dated snapshot must not be treated as timeless.

rules.title: IMO phase-two review of EEXI, SEEMP and CII short-term GHG measures
rules.instrument: MEPC 84 outcome and intersessional work plan

applicability.ship_scope: Ships within the scope of the relevant IMO short-term GHG measures; vessel-specific applicability remains subject to current MARPOL/IMO instruments.
applicability.geographic_scope: International shipping under applicable IMO instruments.
applicability.voyage_scope: Design and annual operational efficiency metrics; route and reporting boundaries depend on the underlying measure.
conditions: Phase-two review includes possible revisions to EEXI, SEEMP and CII measures and consideration of wind propulsion in EEDI/EEXI calculations.
exclusions_or_unknowns: No new WAPS credit formula is established by the review workplan.
Do not treat candidate amendments as current legal requirements.

limitations: This is a review/workplan, not an adopted wind-propulsion credit formula or vessel-specific statutory calculation.

rules.title: Marine diesel engine CH4/N2O measurement and calculation guidelines

applicability.ship_scope: Marine diesel engines and relevant test-bed/onboard measurement programmes, subject to each resolution's detailed scope.
applicability.voyage_scope: Tank-to-wake CH4 and/or N2O measurement and calculation.
conditions: MEPC.415(84) addresses engine-load monitoring and calculation of emission values.
MEPC.416(84) addresses continuous emission monitoring systems.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Do not assume measurement data exists unless suitable calibrated instruments and records are available.
Confirm mandatory/voluntary status and applicable method from the resolution and current IMO instructions.

limitations: Guidelines do not establish that a particular ship's instruments are calibrated or that emissions records have been independently verified.

rules.title: EU Emissions Trading System maritime transport coverage
rules.instrument: Directive 2003/87/EC as amended, including Directive (EU) 2023/959 and maritime implementing provisions
rules.revision_or_resolution: Consolidated text and current Commission guidance must be consulted

applicability.ship_scope: Companies and ships within the EU ETS maritime scope, including applicable ship size/type and reporting requirements.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU/EEA port emissions and voyages with EU port calls, as defined in current law.
applicability.voyage_scope: 100% coverage for voyages between EU ports and emissions within EU ports; 50% coverage for voyages with one end outside the EU, subject to the legal rules.
conditions: Maritime ETS phase-in is 40% for 2024 emissions, 70% for 2025 emissions and 100% from 2026 emissions onward.
CH4 and N2O enter maritime ETS scope from 2026; CO2 was covered earlier.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Applicability, responsible company, ship scope, exemptions and voyage classification must be resolved from legal text and verified facts.

output_scope: EU ETS covered CH4 emissions from 2026
EU ETS covered N2O emissions from 2026

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Aggregate gas-specific emissions by eligible voyage/port segment and reporting year, applying the legally defined coverage share and surrender phase-in. Preserve each gas and the applicable GWP/calculation method.

phase_in.meaning: Surrender phase-in for emissions year 2025, reported/surrendered in 2026
Full phase-in for emissions year 2026 onward

limitations: Surrender phase-in is not the same as the geographic covered-emissions fraction.
Do not apply one fleet-wide coverage ratio to every voyage or period.

rules.title: FuelEU Maritime annual well-to-wake GHG intensity requirement
rules.revision_or_resolution: Use consolidated Regulation and applicable delegated/implementing acts

applicability.ship_scope: Ships and energy use within FuelEU Maritime's vessel, size, company and voyage scope.
applicability.geographic_scope: EU/EEA port and voyage scope as defined in Regulation (EU) 2023/1805.
applicability.voyage_scope: Annual average GHG intensity of energy used on board under the Regulation's well-to-wake boundary.
conditions: The regulation defines yearly reduction factors and specific treatment of eligible fuels/flexibilities.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Verify RFNBO reward, banking, borrowing, pooling, exemptions and verification under current text and acts.
A generic tank-to-wake CO2 factor is not a substitute.

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Calculate annual average well-to-wake GHG intensity of energy used on board using the prescribed fuel pathway, gas and GWP methodology, then compare with the applicable target after reduction factor.

limitations: A regulation calculation is not a verifier statement; all ship scope, fuel pathway and annual energy records must be evidenced.

rules.title: North-East Atlantic Emission Control Area
rules.instrument: MARPOL Annex VI amendment adopted by MEPC 84

applicability.ship_scope: Ships subject to MARPOL Annex VI sulphur requirements while operating within the designated ECA.
applicability.geographic_scope: North-East Atlantic ECA, covering designated EEZs and territorial seas extending up to 200 nautical miles from the baselines of Greenland, Iceland, the Faroe Islands, Ireland, the United Kingdom, France, Spain and Portugal; apply the official adopted coordinates.
applicability.voyage_scope: Voyage legs and port/operational segments within the ECA after the effective application date.
conditions: The amendment enters into force on 1 September 2027.
SOx/PM ECA fuel-sulphur requirements (0.10% m/m) apply from 1 September 2028, following the one-year delay under MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14.6.

NOx Tier III applies to relevant marine diesel engines over 130 kW on ships operating in the ECA where the building contract is placed on or after 1 January 2027; if no building contract, keel laid/on similar stage on or after 1 July 2027; or delivered on or after 1 January 2031.
Ship design/build milestones and route entry date must both be resolved; a single ECA effective date is not sufficient for NOx applicability.
exclusions_or_unknowns: Exact legal scope and coordinates must be read from Resolution MEPC.407(84), its certification/entry-into-force status and charted geographic boundary.
SOx/PM operational sulphur requirements start 1 September 2028, not on the general 1 September 2027 entry-into-force date.
NOx Tier III is construction-date dependent and applies only to relevant engines/ships under MARPOL Annex VI.
This is a local air-pollution requirement, not a lifecycle-GHG factor.

output_scope: NOx Tier III ship-construction-date applicability from ECA entry into force
limitations: Adoption is distinct from application; route geometry alone does not establish fuel compliance.

calculation_contract.formula_or_method: Evaluate route-segment intersection with the official MEPC.407(84) polygon and the voyage date. Evaluate SOx/PM fuel sulphur requirements from 2028-09-01. Separately evaluate NOx Tier III engine/ship applicability against building contract, keel-laying/similar-stage and delivery dates, engine power threshold, and operation in the ECA.

phase_in.meaning: SOx/PM fuel sulphur ceiling 0.10% m/m from 1 September 2028.

rules.instrument: MEPC 84 intersessional work and MEPC 85 agenda
rules.revision_or_resolution: Dated status snapshot as of 10 November 2026

applicability.ship_scope: Proposed global maritime fuel standard and GHG pricing mechanism; final ship/vessel scope is subject to adoption text.
applicability.geographic_scope: Potential global application if formally adopted.
applicability.voyage_scope: Scenario analysis only until adoption and effective dates are established.
conditions: A resumed extraordinary session is provisionally scheduled for 4 December 2026, subject to confirmation.
exclusions_or_unknowns: As of this snapshot, the framework is not formally adopted.
Do not model proposed provisions as current binding liability.

limitations: This snapshot becomes stale after subsequent IMO sessions or decisions; refresh before future use.

rules.title: Draft International Ship Manoeuvrability Standards and goal-based SOLAS steering/propulsion revisions
rules.instrument: SDC 12 outcome and ongoing SOLAS Chapter II-1 (Part C)/Chapter V work
rules.revision_or_resolution: SDC 12, 19–23 January 2026; dated regulatory snapshot 10 November 2026

applicability.ship_scope: Proposed new ISSM intended for new ships subject to draft goal-based SOLAS steering/propulsion regulations; exact ship/type/date scope is not yet adopted.
applicability.geographic_scope: Potential international SOLAS application, subject to final instruments and ratification/entry-into-force terms.
applicability.voyage_scope: Design/manoeuvrability test and trial requirements; future standards are not yet binding.
conditions: SDC 12 continued work on goal-based SOLAS II-1 (Part C) and Chapter V steering/propulsion revisions intended to cover traditional and non-traditional systems.

SDC 12 discussed new International Ship Manoeuvrability Standards for new ships subject to the new goal-based regulations; basic principles were agreed in principle but further technical work was required.
Current roadmap anticipates SDC 13 work in 2027, expected adoption around 2029 and target entry into force 1 January 2032; dates are planned milestones only.
Current MSC.137(76) standards remain the manoeuvrability reference for existing ships under the stated roadmap.
exclusions_or_unknowns: No new ISSM has been adopted as of 10 November 2026.
Do not treat roadmap dates as binding application dates.
Final ship scope, construction-date transition and manoeuvring criteria remain subject to technical and legal development.

limitations: Committee outcome and roadmap do not create a current compliance obligation.
Confirm later SDC/MSC decisions and final text before use.
